attribution.notice: The upstream progression extension read for this entry is authored by BlakeBr0 and published under the MIT licence. It was read at the pinned revision below to write a behaviour specification. Ravel's counterpart is an independent implementation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or derived from the original's source text.

publication.notes: The fetched source lives only in the public repository's ignored fixture tree at tests/fixtures/local/m6-clean-room/ and is not tracked. The specification derived from it is tracked at specifications/m6-foundation/RVL-002.md and is published in-tree in this public repository. The upstream material is not cleared for publication while the names surface is unresolved. The fetched tree includes the entry's binary assets (62 texture files) and its declarative model, block-state, loot, tag, recipe and world-generation documents; the textures were not read as behaviour and nothing is shipped from them.
publication.reviewedBy: structure-reviewed 2026-09-05 by an independent Claude reader that had seen no upstream source; it read the specification first and then the counterpart's module list and public types to see whether a structural noun had crossed, after the counterpart was implemented; verdict: accepted with findings, 5 findings fixed in the specification and the counterpart on 2026-09-05; the specification's read/inferred/unknown markers and closing coverage statement were checked present. No human has read the specification in full.

rights.basis: MIT, read at the source rather than trusted from the inventory. Reading, modification and derivative works are permitted, which is what source-informed reimplementation requires. The counterpart must not copy source text; the specification written from this read carries no upstream identifier, which checks/verify-spec-identifiers.sh was run over and returned no finding.
MIT imposes no behavioural restriction and the inventory records behaviour as cleared and sourceUse as permitted for this entry.

Unchanged from the inventory. MIT does not grant trademark rights, so the project's own name, its mod id and its content identifiers remain unresolved. The specification therefore names nothing after the original, and no save-compatible identifier mapping is specified. This entry makes the constraint sharper than usual: its content is almost entirely catalogue, so an identifier mapping is the one thing a save-compatible counterpart would need and the one thing this record cannot clear.

62 texture files were fetched with the source and not read. The inventory records textures as cleared for this artifact and the licence reserves no asset separately. Nothing upstream is tracked or shipped; any counterpart art is rewritten from reference under policies/source-access.json and recorded in the package's assets-provenance.json.

The fetched tree carries no binary model file; its models are 102 declarative model documents fetched with the source and read only for the registration census the specification records. The inventory records models as cleared for this artifact and the licence reserves no asset separately. Nothing upstream is tracked or shipped.

The fetched tree contains no sound file, which is what the inventory's not-applicable verdict for this artifact holds. The specification refers to sounds only as host sound effects reused by the entry's fluid and block declarations, never as material shipped with it.

No branding material was fetched or read; the display name, logo and author identity are excluded regardless of licence status under policies/source-access.json. The mod descriptor's display name, author, credits, update feed and product page were read only to confirm the dependency and side declarations the specification's section 2 and section 13 state, and none of that text is transcribed.

sources.use: The upstream implementation, fetched as a source archive into the public repository's ignored fixture tree at tests/fixtures/local/m6-clean-room/tar/ and extracted alongside it, and read to write specifications/m6-foundation/RVL-002.md. Version correspondence to the pinned pack artifact -- exact: the build script at this revision declares version '1.21.1-8.0.13' and an archive base name that together produce the pinned artifact file name MysticalAgradditions-1.21.1-8.0.13.jar, and its properties declare the game version 1.21.1. The revision was located by reading the build-script and properties history: the upstream project publishes no tag and no release, keeps one rolling development branch, and began porting that branch to a later game version in the commit immediately after this one, so the 1.21.1 line has no branch of its own and this commit is the last on that branch before the later-version port began. The extracted tree carries a second directory for that later branch of the same project; only the revision-suffixed directory named above was read. No decompilation was performed and no jar was opened.

sources.use: Records the fetch. No fetch tool exists in either repository; the earlier rows were written by hand and this one was fetched with a plain archive download from the same host and appended in the same form, digesting the archive with sha256 as the existing rows do. The digest binds the archive as fetched at the time above rather than asserting that the host re-serves identical bytes. A pre-existing row for this same repository at the rolling branch head remains in the file and names a different commit and digest; it is a different revision and nothing in this record or the specification comes from it.
